dod_intent_evidence: Army-funded $1,149,775 Phase II STTR (Aug 2023) with Battelle Memorial Institute to adapt their FDA-cleared Sparrow device for battlefield acute stress reaction — SBIR abstract and news section.
score_evidence: "Many battlefield situations do not allow for the affected soldier to be close enough to trained personnel to avert adverse effects from an ASR event." → shows real operator/field awareness already present, lowering deployment_awareness_absence and operator_absence per the 'fluent = low score, still a keep' calibration rule

blind_spots.blind_spot: A pre-submission FDA meeting for the battlefield-ASR indication hadn't even started as of the Phase II abstract, separate from the existing opioid-withdrawal 510(k).
blind_spots.operator_reality: Without a completed regulatory pathway specific to the ASR/battlefield indication, the device can't be issued to units regardless of technical readiness — Phase II SBIR funding doesn't confer authority to field.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Team is optimizing the clinical/regulatory track for their core commercial product line; the military indication is a secondary program riding on that infrastructure.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: A pre-submission application will be submitted to the FDA to get feedback on the regulatory strategy and the future clinical study design.

blind_spots.blind_spot: Planned efficacy testing is described only as a 'clinical model of laboratory stress,' not actual field conditions (dust, heat, exertion, combat gear) the device would face if fielded.
blind_spots.operator_reality: 'Operationally relevant' testing done in a lab doesn't validate electrode adhesion, battery life, or signal reliability in the dust/heat/motion conditions an E-5 would actually wear it in — a classic clinical-to-fielded gap.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Company's core competency and infrastructure is FDA clinical trials, not military environmental test protocols.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: test its efficacy to restore performance on operationally relevant tasks in a clinical model of laboratory stress.

blind_spots.blind_spot: The abstract diagnoses the exact problem (proximity to trained personnel) but never says who administers or trains on Sparrow in the field once fielded — no line-medic training or doctrine plan described.
blind_spots.operator_reality: Solving the 'proximity to trained personnel' problem on paper still requires an actual training/doctrine plan for combat medics or self-administration under stress — unaddressed in public materials.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Company's commercial go-to-market motion (facility/provider-administered) doesn't map onto self-administration in a combat environment, and that gap hasn't been worked yet.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: Many battlefield situations do not allow for the affected soldier to be close enough to trained personnel to avert adverse effects from an ASR event.

opener_hook: Spark Biomedical's Army Phase II STTR with Battelle still needs an FDA pre-submission meeting before the battlefield-stress version of Sparrow can begin clinical testing.
what_they_do: Makes an FDA-cleared wearable ear device (tAN) for opioid withdrawal, with a separate Army-funded offshoot to treat acute battlefield stress reactions.
